text:
alex: Heads-up — ran the slotted/coalesce reservoir probe this morning. Seeing weird KV cache hit churn when micro-batch interval jitter > 2ms. Posting quick perf snapshots and config we used.

maria: thanks, can you paste the p95 numbers?

alex: p50: 18ms, p95: 132ms for decode path on rn50-like load. After enabling the reservoir coalesce policy the p95 jumps to 210ms intermittently. p99 spikes to ~520ms for some requests.

sven: are those with the new kernel selector rules (force flash_attn_v2 when seq < 512)?

alex: yes. We flipped kernel selection to prefer flash_attn_v2 for short seqs, fallback to cutlass_fallback when memory pressure spikes. The odd part: when jitter > 2ms we see more cutlass_fallback falls which correlate with KV misses.

tara: can you share the experiment config?

alex: pasted below — it’s the exact job we ran:

```json
{
  "batching": {
    "policy": "slotted_reservoir",
    "micro_interval_ms": 4,
    "coalesce_delay_ms": 1,
    "jitter_ms": 3,
    "token_budget": 1024,
    "headroom_pct": 15
  },
  "kernel_selector": {
    "prefer": ["flash_attn_v2"],
    "fallback": ["cutlass_fallback"],
    "memory_margin_mb": 256
  }
}
```

maria: nice, so micro_interval 4ms + jitter 3ms. That jitter seems high for small windows. What’s the arrival variance?

alex: arrival stddev on that trace ~1.8ms but with periodic clumps from the front-end bursts. We added jitter to de-synchronize but might be over-smoothing and causing reservoir starvation.

ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T10:02:14Z — started canary on 3 nodes (eng-runtime/canary).

sven: hypothesis: when jitter aligns poorly with slotted reservoir boundaries we end up with small micro-batches that still trigger kernel selection but hold onto KV entries longer -> eviction churn. That causes more fallbacks + higher latency.

tara: do we have KV eviction metrics overlaid with kernel flips?

alex: yes — here's the short log extract showing eviction spikes and kernel fallback counts during the window: 

```
[10:02:35] kv_evictions/sec=0.4 fallback_count=3 kernel=flash_attn_v2 -> cutlass_fallback
[10:02:36] kv_evictions/sec=4.8 fallback_count=17 kernel=flash_attn_v2 -> cutlass_fallback
[10:02:37] kv_evictions/sec=6.1 fallback_count=29 kernel=cutlass_fallback
```

maria: that looks like memory pressure windowed into short bursts. Could token_budget be too low for bursts? 1024 tokens may be fine on average but not tail bursts.

sven: try increasing headroom_pct to 30 and token_budget to 1536 in a follow-up canary. Keep micro_interval at 4ms but reduce jitter to 1ms. That should make coalesce timing more deterministic while still avoiding alignment.

alex: will run a canary with:

```json
{"batching":{"micro_interval_ms":4,"coalesce_delay_ms":1,"jitter_ms":1,"token_budget":1536,"headroom_pct":30}}
```

tara: also consider a soft kernel-degrade rule: if fallback_count > 10 in last 30s for a worker, prefer cutlass_fallback proactively. Avoid flip-flopping.

maria: agree — hysteresis on kernel selector would reduce oscillation. Add a cooldown window of 20s after a forced fallback.

ops-bot: canary started (nodes=3) for config hash a1b2c3.

alex: quick results after 10 minutes: p50 19ms, p95 110ms, p99 240ms. KV evictions down 70%. No kernel flip-flop observed.

sven: promising. Any effect on throughput?

alex: throughput stable, slight increase in token/sec due to fewer fallbacks.

maria: let's run a longer 2h run with traffic shaping for bursts. Add an instrumentation trace that tags requests with micro_window_slot_id so we can correlate slot collisions with latencies.

alex: added slot_id tagging, will push trace in next run.

dev-bot: perf-alert: slight regressions detected in a subset of canary pods earlier. Alert suppressed after config change.

tara: follow-up tasks:
- run 2h canary with token_budget=1536 & jitter=1ms
- add kernel hysteresis (cooldown 20s)
- collect slot_id traces + KV eviction overlays
- run kernel selector ablation to measure pure kernel impact (no batching changes)

sven: also add a synthetic microburst workload to test headroom saturation. Use 8 concurrent clients emitting 50-100 short requests in quick succession.

alex: noted. I'll schedule the canary and post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: canary finished (success=3/3) — logs archived to https://internal.redwood/ci/perf/2480001234-canary

maria: great work — this is a good example of batching+kernel interplay. We'll reconvene after the 2h run.

alex: will follow up tomorrow with traces.
